title: TensorHyper-VQC task code sharing
amendment_01: The initial fixed-seed development teacher produced one identical sign-label function for all four task codes, so it did not test logical multiplicity. Development-only seed/scale search selected seed 101608 and TT core scale 2.0 using task-function uniqueness, without inspecting Mirror-vs-control differences. The scorer uses a common JSON header plus contiguous little-endian float32 payload to avoid framework-container overhead dominating this tiny model; header and every tensor are included in byte counts. Initial run is excluded. Gates and fresh seeds are unchanged.
hypothesis: For an aligned task-family generated by one shared TT circuit hypernetwork, a scalar task Givens phase can preserve shot-based classification with fewer actual inference bytes than native rank-2 TT task cores.
physical_object: shared TT cores generating gate angles for a 4-qubit, 2-layer VQC skeleton
mirror_coordinate: one task phase m_t decoded to the rank-2 TT core (cos m_t, sin m_t)
logical_multiplicity: four task-conditioned circuit functions on one physical gate skeleton

development.input_patterns: all sixteen 4-bit basis inputs are scored; no training or tuning data split is used
development.teacher_labels: generated by the fixed aligned TT teacher; score-only
development.selection_metric: task accuracy, teacher-logit agreement, actual serialized inference bytes, logical gate count/depth and shot count

storage.format: common UTF-8 JSON header plus contiguous little-endian float32 arrays; header and all array descriptors included
paid_objects: TT cores or independent angle table
task phase or task latent code

success_gate: Mirror reaches >=98% teacher task accuracy, saves >=10% actual bytes vs native rank-2 TT task cores, and beats ordinary scalar-phase control by >=2 percentage points at matched gates/shots.
failure_gate: Mirror aliases or loses to native scalar-phase control, or misses the quality/bytes gate vs native TT.
boundaries: no hardware compilation or QPU result
